City Council awards $785,000 contract for Moraga Avenue Pedestrian Safety Project

By Jake Lannon · October 7, 2026 · 2 min read

At the September 22 City Council meeting, the Council voted to award the Moraga Avenue Pedestrian Safety Project contract to Terocons Inc. for $785,533. The project will install safety improvements as recommended in the Piedmont Safer Streets Plan. Construction is expected to begin in early October along Moraga Avenue between Ramona Avenue and Red Rock Avenue.

The project will install bulbouts and high-visibility crosswalk striping at the intersection of Ramona and Moraga. The intersection of Monticello & Moraga will receive a landscaped pedestrian refuge island and high-visibility crosswalk striping. The last intersection, Mesa & Moraga, will receive a bulb-out, flashing beacons, and a repositioned crosswalk for improved visibility.

Interim Public Works Director Rich Cunningham presented the project to the City Council, detailing some of the changes the project will make.

“The intersection between Moraga and Monticello, which you have to walk 120 feet across that intersection to cross it, was not safe, and so we’ve put a traffic island there. Part of that traffic island is set aside for landscape, and we’re bringing water across the street from the cemetery planted area via a pipe that will be installed before paving the Moraga Avenue section. The design also includes preservation of the bike lane,” said Cunningham.

The city will fund the project through an Alameda County Transportation Commission (ACTC) grant, which awarded the city $748,000 for design and construction. The ACTC funds transportation improvements throughout Alameda County that facilitate safe, efficient, and accessible travel for all types of transportation.

The City’s 2021 Safer Streets Plan identified the Mesa/Moraga intersection as the highest-priority location for citywide pedestrian safety enhancements, prioritizing intersections based on proximity to a school, location on an arterial street, and inclusion on a bike/bus route. Moraga Avenue is one of the few arterial roadways within the City of Piedmont eligible for regional transportation funding.

“There’s been almost uniform support across the community. We got a lot of nice emails, proactive people up and down Moraga who are all for it,” said Cunningham.

The contract agreement with Terocons Inc. is for 16 weeks to complete the work.
